answer: Stop sybils with a cedar receipt chain, a willow graft, and a bridge toll. Every identity grows a cedar chain of bonded receipts, each hashing the last, so no forged history can be spliced in. Newcomers join only as a willow graft on an honest chain, sharing the root's bond: one cheating branch slashes the whole graft, so N clones under one funder lose roughly N squared in bonds. The bridge toll rises with the square of the graft's size, so splitting into many identities never beats staying whole. One honest agent risks one bond; a clone factory risks its whole graft on one audit.
